S3 event notifications are designed to be delivered at least once, typically in seconds but sometimes a minute or longer

sources.source: Generic File Source Options (Apache Spark docs)

items.item: ignoreCorruptFiles lets Spark jobs continue running when encountering corrupted files, returning only the contents that could be read

A reader that simply lists a landing prefix cannot distinguish a complete batch from a crashed, partial one, measured directly: a producer crashing after thirty-one of forty files leaves a naive reader reporting a number measurably short of the truth, with no error raised anywhere.

A manifest-gated reader checks only for the manifest's own existence, never the data files directly, so an incomplete batch with no manifest is trusted as zero files, not a plausible partial set — the opposite failure mode from a naive listing reader.

An object store's only atomic operation is a single object's own write; there is no rename at all, which is why committing a batch by renaming a staging directory is not a slow version of something safe, it is not an operation available on this kind of storage.

at.step: Reveal: why rename is not the fix

items.item: A plain overwrite lets two producers racing for the same key resolve silently to whichever one runs last, with zero signal that the other's work was discarded; a conditional write using If-None-Match rejects the second producer outright and loudly, measured directly against the identical race.

A poison file is quarantined with the specific reason it failed validation attached, measured directly: one of three landed files fails on its own amount field and is quarantined with that exact reason, while the other two land completely untouched.

Schema-on-write and schema-on-read differ only in timing, not in whether a bug is eventually caught: the identical malformed file is caught at the instant it lands under schema-on-write and left completely unnoticed for dozens of runs under schema-on-read, until the one run that finally reads the broken column, both measured directly.

Event-notification-driven discovery needs its own deduplication because delivery is documented as at-least-once, but its own cost never grows with how many objects already sit under a prefix; listing's own cost keeps climbing with the prefix's size regardless of how many objects are actually new, measured directly across three growing prefix sizes.

Chapter 1 topic 11's own object-storage contract (atomic writes per object, read-after-write consistency, conditional writes, no rename) is the constraint every protocol in this topic is built around, not re-derived independently; Chapter 3 topic 13's idempotent-merge-load pattern is the same deterministic-identity idea the manifest's own role reuses.
